source.title: LipsFormer: Introducing Lipschitz Continuity to Vision Transformers
source.authors: Xianbiao Qi; Jianan Wang; Yi-Hao Chen; Yu-Kai Shi; Lei Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendices; no cut-off or garbling prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own training outcomes, including non-convergence and divergence under some normalization, attention, and residual-weight settings, alongside successful convergence for alternatives. These findings qualify training stability claims, though the experiments use ImageNet Transformers rather than the claim versions’ CIFAR or other specified settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy and training convergence, not training classification error rates or zero-error results on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100. The ImageNet results therefore do not directly test V1–V6 as worded. Relevant own outcomes include ablation results on whether LipsFormer-CSwin converges, plus training-loss observations for LipsFormer-Swin models. Cited prior-work results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual connections and Xavier-based initialization in a new Transformer method, reporting its performance and component ablations. Its own results do not test V1–V6: Transformer convergence and validation accuracy do not measure the specified training-error, local-minimum, plain-network depth, initialization-speed, stability-threshold, or batch-normalization effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present LipsFormer as a Transformer whose Lipschitz-oriented components permit stable ImageNet training without warmup and strong classification accuracy. Their ablations show sensitivity to normalization, attention, and residual scale; all three tested weight initializations converge. These results do not establish V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The work studies Lipschitz-constrained Vision Transformers on ImageNet-1K, using CenterNorm, scaled cosine similarity attention, weighted residual shortcuts, spectral initialization, and DropPath. It does not test the specified random-initialization CIFAR training-error recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: In the 100-epoch LipsFormer-CSwin-T ablation, convergence outcomes vary with normalization, attention formulation, and residual weight α. The paper reports that different convolution blocks and DropPath ratios change accuracy; the text says warmup adds no further improvement in its ablation.

fits_no_version.finding: Without warmup, LayerNorm does not converge, whereas CenterNorm and no normalization converge, reaching 81.6% and 80.3% validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice affects convergence in the tested 100-epoch ImageNet LipsFormer-CSwin-T recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Dot-product attention diverges; L2 attention and SCSA converge with 81.3% and 81.6% validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention formulation affects training stability in this Transformer recipe without warmup.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual scales 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 yield 81.4%, 81.6%, and 81.3% validation accuracy; 0.4 diverges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial residual-branch scale affects convergence in the tested fixed-depth Transformer.

fits_no_version.finding: Truncated normal, Xavier, and spectral initialization all converge, yielding 80.7%, 81.2%, and 81.6% validation accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These initializations produce different final validation accuracies within the tested LipsFormer recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: LipsFormer-Swin-L has lower reported training loss than Base, approximately 2.2 versus 2.5, but lower validation accuracy, 83.5% versus 84.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing LipsFormer-Swin size from Base to Large improves training fit but worsens ImageNet validation accuracy under this recipe.

record.problems: The paper reports ImageNet-1K accuracy rather than training classification error, so convergence and training-loss outcomes do not establish the claim’s near-zero training-error criterion. Ablation outcomes are reported for one model variant and 100 epochs; no uncertainty estimates are given. Some training-loss comparisons are qualitative text descriptions accompanying curves.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible claim-version rows: the reported outcomes concern Transformer stability and accuracy, not the specified versions’ measured behaviors. Other Table 3 ablations for warmup, convolution blocks, and DropPath report accuracy changes but not training error or the convergence/stability outcomes central to the claim; they are not included as rows.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional-network training classification error, including random labels, capacity, early stopping, and regularization effects.
Spurious local minima and extra-student-neuron effects in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training-error degradation in plain convolutional networks, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh networks and very deep convolutions.
Loss and curvature trajectories relative to the initial stability limit, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability behavior, and below-threshold divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on accuracy acquisition speed and learning-rate tolerance, and matched Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern related outcomes outside the claim versions and should not serve as claim-verdict evidence. Their cannot_determine states refer to the named versions, not uncertainty about the explicitly reported convergence outcomes. The paper's assertion that deeper networks require smaller residual scales is not demonstrated by a controlled depth-by-scale experiment.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training error measurements, corrupted or random labels, or comparisons of model size and early stopping.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or student-width sweep.
No plain versus residual convolutional depth comparison on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; the paper studies Transformer components and does not test the stated depth-shortcut comparison.

No plain-network activation-matched initialization, tanh-network, or 10,000-layer convolution experiments. A Transformer initialization ablation is reported, but it does not measure the version’s stated trainable-depth or speed outcomes.
No learning-rate stability-limit, catapult, sharpness, or full-batch squared-loss experiment.
No same-network batch-normalization comparison or accuracy-speed and learning-rate-tolerance measurement; cited work is not this study’s result.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with LayerNorm instead of the paper’s CenterNorm; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The paper defines “Not converge” as training loss oscillating without converging. This measures convergence, not training classification error.
rows.check: LayerNorm non-convergence is correctly reported, but it does not establish absence of any named version; LayerNorm is not batch normalization.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with no normalization; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The text says the no-Norm model successfully converges; this row records its reported accuracy, not training error.
rows.check: 80.3% is validation top-1 accuracy. Successful convergence without normalization does not test the Fixup recipe or the batch-normalization comparison in V6.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with CenterNorm; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The text says CenterNorm and no-Norm both successfully converge, and CenterNorm outperforms no-Norm by 1.3%.
rows.check: 81.6% is validation top-1 accuracy; the CenterNorm comparison does not measure a named version.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with standard dot-product attention; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The paper defines “Diverged” as loss exploding because of NaN or Inf. The text attributes forward value explosion to standard dot-product self-attention.
rows.check: Dot-product attention divergence is correctly reported, but no initial learning-rate stability threshold or subsequent curvature trajectory is measured for V5.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with L2 distance attention; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The authors say SCSA works better than L2 distance attention.
rows.check: 81.3% is validation top-1 accuracy for an attention ablation, not a measure of any named version.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with scaled cosine similarity attention (SCSA); trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The text says SCSA works well under the Lipschitz guarantee.
rows.check: 81.6% is validation top-1 accuracy for the proposed attention method, not a measure of any named version.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with residual weight α initialized to 0.1; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The paper reports this choice converges.
rows.check: 81.4% is validation top-1 accuracy at fixed Transformer depth; residual-scale initialization does not test plain-network initialization speed or trainable depth.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with residual weight α initialized to 0.2; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The paper reports that large α initializations either do not converge or diverge quickly; α values are separately reported in Table 3.
rows.check: 81.6% is validation top-1 accuracy at fixed Transformer depth, outside the named versions.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with residual weight α initialized to 0.3; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The authors describe large α initializations as producing non-convergence or quick divergence; the table reports this value separately.
rows.check: Table 3 reports successful training with 81.3% validation accuracy at α = 0.3. The general prose about large α must not be read as non-convergence for this condition.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with residual weight α initialized to 0.4; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The paper defines “Diverged” as loss exploding because of NaN or Inf.
rows.check: Divergence at α = 0.4 is correctly reported, but the experiment does not measure a named version or compare depths.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with truncated-normal initialization; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The text says all three initializations converge; truncated normal is slightly below spectral and Xavier.
rows.check: 80.7% is validation accuracy, and all three initializations converge. This residual Transformer comparison measures neither learning speed nor maximum trainable depth in plain networks.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with Xavier initialization; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The text says all three initializations converge; spectral and Xavier slightly outperform truncated normal.
rows.check: 81.2% is validation accuracy; convergence with Xavier initialization alone does not test V4's comparative speed or depth effect.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-CSwin-Tiny
rows.operation_detail: Ablation with spectral initialization; trained without learning-rate warmup.
rows.note: The authors state spectral initialization has better Lipschitz interpretability than Xavier; the accuracy is reported in the ablation table.
rows.check: 81.6% is validation accuracy; spectral initialization's accuracy advantage does not establish V4's learning-speed or trainable-depth effect.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-Swin-L
rows.stage_stated: training loss described during ImageNet-1K training; full schedule is 300 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Training loss compared with LipsFormer-Swin-B during training.
rows.note: The paper says LipsFormer-Swin-L shows obvious overfitting; its training loss is smaller while its test accuracy is lower.
rows.check: The approximately 2.2 training loss is correctly reported, but loss under this ImageNet Transformer recipe cannot establish near-zero CIFAR training classification error.

rows.subject: LipsFormer-Swin-B
rows.stage_stated: training loss described during ImageNet-1K training; full schedule is 300 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Training loss compared with LipsFormer-Swin-L during training.
rows.note: The paper says the larger LipsFormer-Swin-L has lower training loss but lower test accuracy than LipsFormer-Swin-B.
rows.check: The approximately 2.5 training loss is correctly reported, but this reciprocal comparator does not measure any named version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
